To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new reactor for the continuous retention of NAPD(H) with noncharged ultrafiltration membranes and we applied it to obtain simultaneously glucone and glutamate by coupled enzyme reactions.
we developed a new reactor configuration that allows to obtain simultaneously two products by coupling two enzymes in a single reactor.

the combination of ultrafiltration membranes and polyethyleneimine allows to achieve continuous retention of the native coenzyme NADP(H), even in the presence of high concentrations of glucose and glutamate, which are the main reaction products of the coupled enzyme reactions studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new reactor configurations based on membrane separation technology for the continuous regeneration of NAD(H) and NADP(H).

a new concept of membrane enzyme reactor for continuous retention and recycling of NADP in a low salt environment, which is applicable to many enzyme processes requiring NAD(P)H. (C) 2001 Elsevier Science B.V. All
the design of a new type of enzyme membrane reactor for continuous coenzyme retention and coenzyme regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this reactor is a new concept that could be applicable for the production of several coenzyme-dependent enzymes, in a continuous way, and with a simple design.

the proposed reactor system is an efficient and simple method for continuous production of gluconate and/or glutamate by coupling glucose dehydrogenation and glutamate deamination, using the native coenzyme NADP + and the halophilic glucose dehydrogenases and glutamate dehydrgenases.

the reactor proposed is a very useful tool for the continuous production of gluconate and other NADPH-dependent products, and for other NAD(P)H-dependent enzymes that require a high ionic strength medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactor design and the use of PEI allow to obtain high productivity for the desired product, with a high coenzyme retention, and without the need of a coenzyme recycling system.
the membrane reactor configuration allows the continuous retention of NAdP(H) and the production of gluconate and/or glutamate in high yields.
the use of PEI as a membrane additive is an efficient way to retain native NADP + and NADPH in an enzyme membrane bioreactor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ultrafiltration membranes for continuous coenzyme retention in enzyme membrane reactors is possible when the coenzyme is non-charged.

the use of ultrafiltration membrane reactors is a very attractive alternative to the use of immobilized enzyme reactors for the production of high value-added chemicals, especially in the case of coenzyme-dependent enzymes.

the continuous regeneration of NAD(P)H can be achieved with non-charged membranes, and this opens the possibility of using ultrafiltration membranes in the construction of membrane reactors for NAD(P) regeneration.
